display.purpose: The name on the hero panel and nothing else. Archivo at its widest (wdth 122), weight 900, uppercase.

headline.purpose: Section headings and the footer wordmark. Archivo wdth 118, uppercase, negative tracking.

title.purpose: Station panel headings (wdth 108) and project title plates / direct-contact heading (wdth 112). Uppercase.

body.purpose: All sentences. Archivo unexpanded at wdth 100, capped at the 58ch measure.

label.purpose: Barlow Condensed uppercase at 0.14em. Nav, buttons, chips, field labels, sub-legends, footer heads, interchange text.

data.purpose: Barlow Condensed at weight 700 / 0.1em. Year chips, the interchange year, the portrait tag — the numeral voice.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Standard plate-on-ground cast shadow: station panels, screenshot frames, the interchange band.

shadows.name: lift-lg
shadows.purpose: The hero portrait plate only — the most forward object on the page.

shadows.name: dot
shadows.purpose: Station dots, so a bullet reads as a fixture mounted on the track.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Form fields at focus, alongside a yellow border. A focus indicator, not depth — the only non-cast shadow permitted.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the two line tracks scale up from scaleY(0) on approach. Work track delayed 0.18s behind study.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every other transition — colour, border-colour, background and small transforms on hover, focus and pressed states.

motion.name: nudge-x
motion.purpose: Destination chips and profile rows move along the line on hover, never up off it.

motion.name: nudge-y
motion.purpose: Primary buttons only; returns to 0 on :active. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
This is a public-transport wayfinding system asked to carry one engineer's career. Everything borrows from Massachusetts civic signage: deep navy enamel panels bolted onto a concrete-grey ground, a tactile yellow edge along the platform, coloured route bands that mean something, and timetable rules setting dates in condensed caps. Nothing here is a card grid and nothing is a dark terminal. A visitor reads the page the way they read a station: find the colour, follow the line, arrive at the destination.

The density is that of real signage — generous air around a small number of very confident, very large elements, then tight, tabular data inside each panel. The register is institutional rather than personal: authoritative, plain, no persuasion in the ornament. Depth comes from material, not from software convention. A panel is a physical plate with a hard coloured edge and a shadow it casts on the ground; it is never a floating rounded rectangle with a soft glow. There are no gradients anywhere in the build, and none may be introduced.

The system is deliberately narrow so it stays hand-editable forever: two typefaces from Google Fonts loaded by <link>, one stylesheet, one script, no npm and no bundler. Every rule must be achievable in plain HTML and CSS on GitHub Pages, because that is the whole delivery mechanism.
keyCharacteristics: Navy enamel panels (ink) on a concrete ground (ground), with a tactile yellow platform edge at 14px
Four route colours that are functional labels, not decoration: red projects, orange work, green study, blue contact
Archivo's variable wdth axis genuinely worked — 122 down to 100 as type size falls
Barlow Condensed reserved entirely for timetable data: years, legends, chips, nav, buttons
Hard rectangles everywhere; the only curve in the system is a route bullet
Authored inline SVG pictograms at a single 2.25 stroke weight; no icon font, no icon library
One authored motion moment in the entire page, and it defaults to finished

rules.name: The Route Colour Rule
rules.body: A colour names a destination; it never decorates. Red is projects, orange is work, green is study, blue is contact. If a new element cannot be assigned to one of those four, it takes navy or yellow. Adding a fifth hue means adding a fifth destination.

rules.name: The Bullet Inheritance Rule
rules.body: Route colour enters a subtree exactly once, as style="--bullet: var(--red)" on the section or link. Every child — the head rule, the route bullet, the button's underline, the link underline, the list marker — reads var(--bullet). Never hard-code a route hex on a descendant.

rules.name: The Yellow-Is-Not-A-Route Rule
rules.body: Yellow marks the tactile edge, focus on navy, the current position, and the interchange. It never labels a section and never competes with a route colour for meaning.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Archivo speaks; Barlow Condensed labels. Nothing that is a sentence is set in Barlow Condensed, and nothing that is a date, a legend, a chip, a nav item or a button is set in Archivo. There is no third face and no italic anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The Width-Follows-Scale Rule
rules.body: Archivo's wdth axis widens as type gets larger and narrows as it gets smaller: 122 at the name, 118 at section heads and the wordmark, 112 at plates, 108 at station headings, 100 for prose. Never set a heading at 100, and never expand body copy.

rules.name: The Caps-Are-Signage Rule
rules.body: Uppercase means the text is signage or data — headings, labels, chips, buttons, years. Body copy is never uppercased and never letter-spaced.

rules.name: The Corridor Rule
rules.body: Everything in the line section measures from 42.5% — tracks, dots, panel columns, distance ticks. Move that number and all four move together; never nudge one carrier independently.

rules.name: The Empty-Lane Rule
rules.body: The lane without a station in it is still corridor, not margin. It carries the distance tick for that row, and the corridor is narrowed to 1080px so the lane stays legible as track.

rules.name: The No-Halo Rule
rules.body: Every depth shadow has downward offset and negative spread. No centred glows, no 0 0 Npx ambient rings, no gradients — not in a background, not in an overlay, not in an SVG.

rules.name: The Border-Carries-Structure Rule
rules.body: If an element needs to read as a separate physical object, give it a hard border in ink or its route colour before you reach for a shadow. Shadow lifts a plate that is already framed; it never substitutes for the frame.

rules.name: The Square-Except-Bullets Rule
rules.body: Zero radius on everything that holds content. The only curved things in the system are route bullets and station dots, which are always full circles, never pills. The 2px on the global focus ring is the sole tolerated exception, and it exists so the ring does not read as a fifth border style.

rules.name: The Muted-Carrier Rule
rules.body: Tracing one line desaturates exactly four things on the other: the track, the station dot, the panel's top rule, and the year chip. Text colour, size, weight and position never change. Colour is the only channel the interaction is allowed to touch.

rules.name: The Drawn-By-Default Rule
rules.body: The finished state is the CSS default. The draw-from-zero rule is scoped to .js .line:not(.is-drawn), and the js class is set by an inline script, so no-JS, failed-script and reduced-motion visitors all get the completed diagram rather than an empty corridor. Any future animation must be built the same way round.

dos: Do assign route colour once with style="--bullet: var(--green)" on the section or link and let every descendant read var(--bullet).
Do use Archivo for anything that is a sentence or a heading and Barlow Condensed for anything that is a label, a date, a chip or a button.
Do widen Archivo's wdth axis as type scales up — 108 at station headings, 118 at section heads, 122 at the name — and leave prose at 100.
Do frame a plate with a hard border (6px route colour on top, 6px ink around images, 14px yellow at the page edges) before considering a shadow.
Do keep the focus ring ink on the light ground and yellow on navy; yellow reads at roughly 1.2:1 against concrete and is not a visible indicator there.
Do author new icons as inline <symbol> entries in the sheet at stroke-width: 2.25, 24x24, round caps and joins, fill="none", currentColor.
Do ship every animation with its finished state as the CSS default, gated behind the js class.
Do cap prose at the measure token; long-form paragraphs get a line length, signage lines get max-width: none.
donts: Don't use a gradient anywhere — background, overlay, border or SVG. The build has zero and the material is enamel, which is flat.
Don't round a container, chip, field or button. Circles are for route bullets only, and pills are not part of this system.
Don't introduce a fifth accent hue. Five signal colours exist because five things need naming; a sixth needs a destination first.
Don't set Signal Orange as text on the concrete ground — use the deepened orange-ink variant.
Don't change text colour, size or weight when a filter or focus state changes. Mute the colour carriers only.

Don't add an icon font, an icon package, or an icon. The symbol sheet is the whole vocabulary; the two filled brand marks (GitHub, LinkedIn, X) are a deliberate second tier and the only filled glyphs allowed.
Don't put inside an SVG that is loaded through — it is an isolated document and cannot reach the page webfonts. Set the lettering in HTML over the plate.
Don't introduce anything that requires npm, a bundler, a framework or a Pages Action. Every rule above has to survive a plain git push.
Don't promote a second animated moment. The track draw is the page's one authored gesture; adding a second spends what makes it read as authored.
